To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduction of two Co(III) complexes by Fe(II) in a microemulsion is affected by the location of the complexes within the microemulsion.
the reduction rates of two cobalt complexes, [Co(dip)2]-and [Co(edta)(3-)]-, with similar redox potential were dramatically different in water and in RM microemulsion.
the reduction of cobaltate(III)-complexes is switched off by confinement in a dynamic microheterogeneous environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the control of electron transfer reactions in microemulsion media.
how to control electron-transfer reactions in confined media and how to use the microemulsion to control the reaction pathways of redox reactions.
the development of a new strategy to switch on and off electron transfer reactions by compartmentalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the redox reaction between [Co(edta)(2-)](-) and [Fe(CN)(6)](4-) is switched off by confinement in the RM whereas that between [Co(dipc)(2)(2-)] and [Fe(Cn)(6)](3-) is switched on.

the reduction rates are affected by the location of the reactants within the RM, which is a result of the different sizes and charges of the reactants and the different solvation of the reactants in the different environments.
the reduction of [Co(II)](edta)](-) by hexacyonoferrate(2-) is turned off in the reverse micelle system, whereas the reaction of hexacyanoferrat(2-) with [Co(II)(dipic)(2)(-)] is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of a redox couple can be switched off by either the redox potential of one reactant or by the reactants being located in different compartments.
the reduction of [Co(III)] complexes by hexacyanferrate(II), which are switched on in water, are switched off by confinement in RM media.

the reduction of [Co(III) complexes] by hexacyaniferrate(II), which is a model for electron-transfer reactions, was switched off or switched on by the confinement of the reactants within a microemulsion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to control the redox reactions in a microemulsion system through the choice of reactants and their redox potentials.
compartmentalization can be used to switch off redox reactions in a dynamic microenvironment, and this is an important step toward the design of artificial enzymes.

the redox reactions of [Co(dpp)](3+) (dpp is 4,7-diphenyl-1,10-phenanthroline), [Co(dip)2](2-) (dip is 2,6-diacetylpyridine dianil) and [Co(edda)](-) (edda is ethylenediaminediacetic acid) are switched off by confinement in the reverse micelles.
